title: Tunnel Radio Infrastructure
summary: A tunnel operator drives a small radio-linked sign board. Learners begin by reading tuned traffic, then progress into tuning, denial-of-service observation, and controlled packet injection.
situation: This context teaches the first contested-spectrum idea: RF output is visible to anyone in range, and weak signalling can be observed, jammed, or overwritten inside a controlled local simulation.
planned_subtasks: Add a larger sign-board state machine with message history and operator acknowledgement.
Add a generated GNU Radio OOK flowgraph matching the sign-board packets.
Add a C packet encoder so developers can modify framing and payload format.

title: Broadcasting Song Metadata
summary: A local broadcaster sends song and advisory metadata on a low-rate side channel. Learners read, tune, disrupt, and inject metadata frames.
situation: This context uses an approachable broadcast story to show how plain RF-origin data can become software input, console output, and ultimately a trust-boundary problem.
planned_subtasks: Add an audio side-channel variant where metadata is hidden inside a tone burst.
Add a small metadata parser binary with safe and unsafe builds.
Add a receiver console printout that mirrors the spreadsheet evidence requirement.

title: Weather Broadcast Boring Voice
summary: A plain voice weather broadcast moves into predictable hopping and then digital audio metadata. Learners recover callsigns, identify weak hopping, and reverse metadata handling.
situation: This context bridges audio radio operations and reverse engineering: the learner must reassemble enough of the RF/audio path to make a simulated receiver act on warning metadata.
planned_subtasks: Add downloadable IQ recordings for every hop segment.
Add a Python hopping-receiver template with TODO sections.
Add a visible warning light and siren widget for the metadata trigger.

title: Civilian Emergency Radio Audio Network
summary: A public-facility announcement network sends short audio bursts across frequencies. Learners recover messages, predict weak pseudorandom hops, and submit valid warning audio.
situation: This is the more operational audio network: participants recover an emergency call, reason about weak hopping state, then use reverse-engineered metadata to activate the simulated public-address receiver.
planned_subtasks: Add a second callsign on Q and I for optional bonus analysis.
Add an exported sample file from the tuned receiver for offline scripting.
Add a receiver-side C integrity check exercise.

title: Bushfire Command and Control
summary: A bushfire sensor/relay network introduces firmware reverse engineering, HDL review, crafted command packets, remote-code-execution style behaviour, and spoofing/null-steering logic.
situation: This advanced context is where the CTF becomes serious: RF-derived command packets interact with embedded code, hardware logic, anomaly detection, and distributed receiver behaviour.
planned_subtasks: Add a compiled stripped firmware target and a safe source build.
Add a HDL testbench runner with waveform output.
Add a propagation/null-steering visualiser for receiver trust decisions.

title: Farm Gates
summary: A rural gate system uses long-range maintenance traffic, embedded admin logic, HDL control paths, and packet-driven actuation. Learners reverse, exploit, and spoof the local simulation.
situation: This context keeps the rural long-range story but structures it around firmware, hardware logic, remote actuation, and spoofed authority in a synthetic local target.
planned_subtasks: Add a gate animation that reflects command timing and lock state.
Add a bitstream patching exercise with a visible super-user logic state.
Add a log-removal/kill-switch defensive write-up comparing safe controller design.
